title: textContent vs innerHTML
learningObjectives: Explain textcontent vs innerhtml and apply safe browser programming practices.

understand.concept: textContent reads or writes the text content of a node without parsing markup. innerHTML reads or parses the HTML markup inside an element and can create DOM nodes from a string. Setting innerHTML with untrusted data creates an injection risk.
understand.whyItMatters: Choosing the correct property makes rendering safer and more predictable. Use DOM methods for structured content and only use sanitized HTML when rich markup is truly required.
understand.analogy: textContent treats angle-bracket content as words; innerHTML treats it as instructions for building elements.
understand.analogyLimit: The analogy is simplified; browser APIs, security boundaries, and accessibility requirements are defined by web platform standards.

explain.narrative: The first line displays the whole string literally. The DOM method version creates a real strong element without interpreting untrusted markup.

examples.explanation: The first line displays the whole string literally. The DOM method version creates a real strong element without interpreting untrusted markup.

questions.prompt: Which property parses a string as HTML markup?
questions.explanation: innerHTML parses and sets markup inside an element.
